scheduler.state: waiting for the pg:lock:scheduler TTL to expire, then starts on its own
scheduler.note: the lock is now held by 36d72900e250:1, which is THIS container's own hostname, so the previous holder is gone and only its TTL is left. The TTL was renewed once by the old process during the first promote (LOCK_HOLDER_TTL_SECONDS = 900, renewal every 5 minutes), which is why the takeover takes up to 15 minutes rather than 15 seconds. `docker compose up -d --no-deps scheduler` does not recreate an already-current container, so a `docker restart puregamma-ai-scheduler-1` is needed once the key is free. Self-healing, no data impact, and the worker — which runs the actual scheduled tasks — is up and connected.

all_services_aligned.scope_precision: All four promoted services carry source 15f7b9d5, and the api/worker/scheduler images are literally the same image ID. This is the first release in the recent series where the frontend and backend are the same commit.

defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.found_by: live browser acceptance against production (the stubbed e2e could not see it — it stubs the upload)
defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.was: a 1x1 PNG upload answered 400 ATTACHMENT_INVALID. Every image was pushed through exif_transpose/convert('RGB')/save(JPEG, quality=88), and that round trip fails on a valid tiny file, so ordinary icons and phone screenshots were rejected while ordinary photographs worked.
defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.now: an image already inside the 2048px budget, already in PNG or JPEG, and without an EXIF orientation is stored byte-for-byte; everything else keeps the downscale-into-JPEG path; a decoder failure is translated into ATTACHMENT_INVALID so a bad upload answers 400 rather than 500.
defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.verified_on: the live site after re-release, and by tests/unit/test_chat_workspace.py

defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.found_by: running the real stream generator in a test instead of a mocked tool path
defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.was: tool_permission returned 'ask' for anything not on the read-only allowlist, and the research plan schedules generate_order_preview and run_nautilus_backtest, so a plain question about BTC stopped for a confirmation card — or, once unknown tools became a refusal, would have failed the turn with READ_ONLY_PERMISSION.
defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.now: the two read-only-by-construction tools are named on the allowlist, and the ask decision is reserved for tools explicitly classified as stateful (STATEFUL_TOOLS, empty today because nothing in the registry mutates state).

defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.was: _context_messages walked messages newest-first and `continue`d past any turn that did not fit the budget, so a conversation with large attachments could answer a question the model never received — silently.
defects_found_and_fixed_this_release.now: the window is built oldest-first and trimmed from its oldest end, the newest turn is exempt from trimming, and any trim is announced to the model in a system message instead of vanishing.

what_shipped: per-conversation permission mode that actually restricts tool execution (read-only refuses, workspace-write confirms only reviewed stateful tools, full-access requires an explicit acknowledgement)

tool-call confirmations: a run stops, the pending call is returned with the conversation, approval is per call, expires after 120 s, is single-use and owner-scoped
composer rebuilt around an attachment tray, a permission selector and a research-settings disclosure, in both themes at 393px and 1280px
attachments survive reloads and reappear in history with their stored cards

not_shipped_on_purpose.x_login_and_dm_bot: uncommitted work in the working tree (apps/api/routers/x_auth.py, x_bot.py, the X settings in config.py, x_inbound_tasks in packages/database/session.py). The frontend half of X sign-in is already on main, so this release is the first that does not accidentally carry the backend half either. known_issues: scheduler waits out the pg:lock:scheduler TTL before it starts (see services.scheduler.note); self-healing, no data impact, and the worker runs the tasks meanwhile

the API rate limiter keys on the peer address it sees, which in production is the Caddy container rather than the visitor, so API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=120 and EXPENSIVE_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=20 are effectively per-deployment budgets rather than per-client ones. Writes (attachment uploads, agent runs) share a 20/min ceiling across all users. Pre-existing and unchanged by this release; it surfaced only because acceptance testing made bursts of uploads and correctly received 429. Worth its own change: forward a trusted client address from Caddy and key on that.

rollback.note: the first attempt at recording a pin copied the build directory's override file, which already carried the NEW pins, so it recorded the release as its own rollback target. The file was replaced and the deploy script now reads the pins off the live containers instead.
rollback.procedure: bash /puregamma/release-rollback.sh /puregamma/override-20260913T180850Z-before-15f7b9d5.yml — it verifies every pinned tag exists locally before it changes anything, then brings api, web, worker and scheduler up on the old pins.
rollback.database: NOT rolled back and does not need to be: 0032 is additive and forward-only. The previous api image (044effcf) does not know about agent_attachments, permission_mode or the approval columns, ignores them, and keeps serving. Rolling the schema back is explicitly refused by the migration's downgrade.
rollback.residual_risk: rolling back to 7ca5ba86 / 044effcf restores the old composer, so attachments become inline text again and the permission selector disappears; files already uploaded stay in the database and become unreachable until the new image returns. Roll back past 6a9e924f and the small-image defect comes back with it.
